title: Answers to onko possession questions with singular owners
summary: Answer possession questions about singular owners with fixed on or ei ole.
objectives: Answer possession questions about singular owners with fixed on or ei ole.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Answer possession questions about singular owners with fixed on or ei ole.
On. or Kyllä, on. confirms possession. Ei ole. or Ei, ei ole. denies it. The owner does not change these verb replies.
keyPoints: Answer possession questions about singular owners with fixed on or ei ole.

examples.english: Do I have a ball? — I do have it.
steps: minulla means “I as the owner”. The question names pallo (“a ball”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.

examples.english: Do you have a book? — You do not have it.
steps: sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person. The question names kirja (“a book”).
The reply denies possession, so use fixed Ei ole (“do/does not have” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.

examples.english: Does she have a dog? — She does have it.
steps: hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”. The question names koira (“a dog”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
Kyllä (“yes”) is an optional answer particle; On. alone also confirms possession.

examples.english: Do I have a cat? — I do have it.
steps: minulla means “I as the owner”. The question names kissa (“a cat”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
Kyllä (“yes”) is an optional answer particle; On. alone also confirms possession.

examples.finnish: Onko hänellä peli? — Ei, ei ole.
examples.english: Does he or she have a game? — No.
steps: The owner does not have the thing: use ei ole.
The optional answer word does not change the fixed verb reply.

commonMistakes: Answer the stated fact: On confirms possession and Ei ole denies it.
Kyllä can accompany an affirmative verb reply; an additional Ei can introduce a negative reply. Keep the verb reply when the task requests it.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Reply to “Onko minulla kynä?” with “I do have it.” Use a verb reply; Kyllä or Ei is optional. kynä means “pen”.
practiceExercises.explanation: Answer the stated possession meaning: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies having it. Both remain fixed with every owner. An optional Kyllä or Ei can introduce the reply.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: fixed possession verb reply; owner and thing understood from the question

parts.formation: Kyllä means “yes”; it can introduce the affirmative verb reply.
Echo fixed on: the owner and thing are understood from the question.

answerDiagnostics.category: Possession question short answers: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Olen and en ole describe “I am” and “I am not”. A possession reply echoes fixed on or ei ole.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Reply to “Onko sinulla peli?” (“Do you have a game?”, one person). Repair “En ole.” (“I am not.”) to mean “No, I do not have it.” Use a possession verb reply; leading Ei is optional.
practiceExercises.explanation: The fact denies possession. Use fixed ei ole, not the personal reply en ole (“I am not”).
practiceExercises.misconceptionCategory: Possession question short answers: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.translation: No, I do not have it.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: fixed ei ole; owner and thing understood from the question

parts.formation: After ei, use fixed ole. A leading Ei (“no”) is optional.

answerDiagnostics.category: Possession question short answers: form or meaning confused
answerDiagnostics.explanation: En ole means “I am not”. The question asks about possession: reply Ei ole (“I do not have it”).
